HW3 — факты для индивидуального отчёта

Протокол

FAR-Trans. 500 warm-пользователей с профилем и хотя бы одной допустимой покупкой до cutoff 2021-06-01. Сортировка по SHA-256 строки 42:<user_id> с вторичным ключом user_id. Первые 100 совпадают с когортой HW2. Период оценки [2021-06-01, 2021-07-01), 30 дней. 62 пользователя имеют непустую цель, 438 — пустую. Пользователи выбирались по данным до cutoff. Будущие Buy использовались как цели при оценке.

Вселенная содержит 767 активов с доступными к cutoff метаданными и положительной исторической ценой. Цель пользователя — множество допустимых ISIN, купленных в окне оценки. Starter исключает точные дубли транзакций и строки восстановленных начальных позиций. Повторная рекомендация ранее купленного актива разрешена.

MaxSim, MeanSim и LLMRank получают один и тот же упорядоченный Top-50 CBF из starter для каждого пользователя. Их списки оценивались на полном наборе релевантных активов, включая цели вне пула. Исходный Top-10 CBF — первые 10 элементов этого пула. Остальные классические baseline используют свою исходную область starter.

Бинарный nDCG@10 с логарифмическим дисконтом. Основная оценка — макросреднее по всем 500 с нулём для пустой цели. Дополнительно — макросреднее по 62 непустым целям. Параметры и хеши сохранены в results/final_results/protocol.json.
SHA-256 протокола d8b0a946f0fc416583234ccef77633c69a3f37f5734733d050b0e524ad44f57d
SHA-256 упорядоченной когорты ec454c5459f8ef526652178408d26793671a1e55da0f8b393e1edcc4e0c80f2c
SHA-256 упорядоченных пулов 068d9c60e6ccaa65f37f266ba5a6f2cc68bac69a65820effb39caccd3dc92e57

Модели и настройки

MaxSim и MeanSim. Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, ревизия 97b0c614be4d77ee51c0cef4e5f07c00f9eb65b3. MPS, FP16, SDPA, batch 8, левый padding, окно 8192, seed 42, 4 потока PyTorch. Пулинг последнего непустого токена, 1024 компоненты, L2-нормализация и косинусные оценки в FP32. Общий кэш по точному тексту признаков. Текст содержит название, категорию, подкатегорию, сектор, отрасль и рынок. История — до пяти последних различных купленных активов. Сортировка по убыванию оценки после округления до шести знаков. При равенстве сохраняется исходный CBF-порядок.

MaxSim берёт максимум косинусной близости кандидата к отдельным активам истории. Абляция MeanSim меняет агрегацию на косинусную близость к L2-нормализованному невзвешенному среднему эмбеддингов истории. Выбор пользователей, кандидаты, тексты, эмбеддинги и метрика общие.

LLMRank. Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B, ревизия 70d244cc86ccca08cf5af4e1e306ecf908b1ad5e. MPS FP16. Используется преподавательский промпт с профилем, числами прошлых Buy, последними 15 событиями Buy и 50 кандидатами в исходном CBF-порядке. Перемешивание выключено. Greedy decoding, do_sample=False, thinking=False, контекст 8192, до 512 новых токенов. Требуется JSON-массив из десяти различных исходных ISIN. При невалидном ответе или превышении контекста используется исходный Top-10 CBF. CPU fallback отключён. Протокол фиксирует torch 2.11.0, transformers 4.57.6, tokenizers 0.22.2. Снимки моделей загружались из локального кэша. Точная версия macOS, модель чипа и сборка Python полного прогона в его артефактах не записаны. Требование среды проекта — Python 3.12.

Итоги nDCG@10

Метод                       Все 500                62 с непустой целью
Popularity                  0.031009900307155794   0.25007984118674026
Latest buy                  0.049486358280213895   0.39908353451785394
Latest buy or sell          0.050318457086664124   0.40579400876342037
CBF                         0.03225811676059308    0.26014610290800866
MaxSim                      0.034070143704655234   0.274759223424639
MeanSim                     0.03439070244539912    0.2773443745596703
LLMRank с CBF fallback      0.031789444699846084   0.2563664895148878

Основное сравнение MaxSim − CBF по всем пользователям +0.001812026944062154. Абляция MaxSim − MeanSim по всем −0.000320558740743886, по непустым −0.0025851511350313. Из 62 непустых целей MaxSim выигрывает у 6 пользователей, проигрывает у 8, равен у 48. Это описательное сравнение. У Latest buy or sell максимальный средний результат среди семи методов.

Failure analysis — наблюдения

Использовано 1, 2–3 и 4–5 исторических активов соответственно у 209, 131 и 160 пользователей. Непустых целей в этих группах 7, 7 и 48. nDCG@10 на непустых у MaxSim / MeanSim: 0.4348 / 0.4348, 0.4982 / 0.4498 и 0.2188 / 0.2292. Для одного актива Top-10 обоих методов совпал у всех 209 пользователей. Победы / поражения / равенства MaxSim на непустых по группам: 0 / 0 / 7, 1 / 1 / 5, 5 / 7 / 36. По двум коротким группам мало оценочных случаев для вывода о влиянии длины истории.

В пулах CBF представлены 42 из 153 релевантных пар «пользователь–актив». Соответственно, 111 пар вне Top-50, это 53 уникальных ISIN, хотя бы раз отсутствующих в пуле. У 40 пользователей пропущена хотя бы одна цель, у 28 все цели. У 5 пользователей цель была в пуле, но оба embedding-метода получили нулевой nDCG@10. Отсутствие цели в Top-50 ограничивает любой reranker на фиксированном пуле. При наличии цели в пуле конкретные промахи подтверждаются её позициями, а причины предпочтений пользователя по журналам не определяются.

83 из 153 релевантных пар — покупки ранее купленных активов. Число повторных рекомендаций из 5000 мест в Top-10 каждого метода: CBF 1017, MaxSim 1005, MeanSim 1009, LLMRank 985, Popularity 910, Latest buy 1606, Latest buy or sell 1590. Повтор определяется по всей допустимой Buy-истории до cutoff. Анонимизированные случаи A–D сохранены в outputs/failure_examples.json.

LLMRank. 494 генерации, 384 валидных ответа, 0 записанных исправлений, 116 fallback из 500. Сохранённые причины: ISIN вне пула 87, дубликаты 18, нарушение требования о десяти строковых ISIN 5, превышение контекста до генерации 6. В финальных checkpoints 0 технических ошибок. Статистика относится к сохранённому финальному состоянию каждого пользователя. Оценка LLMRank включает все fallback.

Время

11.613044958095998 с — заполнение кэша эмбеддингов, включая загрузку модели. 447 уникальных текстов, 0 попаданий в кэш и 447 промахов.
1.4826946309767663 с — совместное ранжирование MaxSim и MeanSim по сохранённому замеру.
9062.023897704436 с — сумма wall-time LLMRank по 500 случаям. Замер внутри `rank_one` включает проверку контекста и ответа, исключает загрузку модели и запись checkpoint.
9056.143112918828 с — сумма внутренних замеров вызовов генерации в преподавательском runtime по 494 ответам.
3.0235639999154955 с — повторная подготовка данных и входов для анализа в Codex. Длительность исходной подготовки, отдельное время загрузки LLMRank, чистое время вычисления эмбеддингов и полное wall-clock время финального прогона отдельно не сохранены.

Личная проверка Ивана Никулина

«Я самостоятельно пересчитал nDCG@10 для CBF (0.317194), MaxSim (0.416181) и MeanSim (0.636439). Все значения совпали с сохранёнными.» U01 — первый случай в порядке когорты среди последних 400 пользователей, где MeanSim превосходит MaxSim. Данные и ранее сохранённые ответы находятся в outputs/manual_check/.

Автоматические проверки Codex

Codex сопоставил сообщённые значения U01 с сохранёнными показателями до шести знаков. В полном эксперименте автоматически сверены хеши исходников, данных, протокола, промптов и входов эмбеддингов, 500 упорядоченных пулов, 3500 пар «пользователь–метод» и 500 checkpoints.      1	# FAR-Trans: Encoder and Ranker baselines
     2	
     3	This package provides two runnable open-weight LLM methods, **adaptations rather
     4	than full paper reproductions**, with the [starter](../far-trans/README.md)'s four
     5	baselines and evaluation unchanged. These are optional starting points: use the
     6	approach relevant to your research question, not necessarily both. Identify your
     7	own change and contribution; improvement over the baselines is not required.
     8	
     9	- **Encoder:** paraphrase each asset's supplied attributes, combine original and
    10	  generated text as separate TF-IDF views, then match assets to a user's past Buy
    11	  history. Compare `llmrec_encoder` with `original_text_cbf`. Inspired by LLM-Rec's
    12	  basic `p_para` prompt; this uses TF-IDF instead of its text encoder/trained MLP.
    13	- **Ranker:** show the LLM past Buy counts, dated recent purchases, the explicit
    14	  most recent Buy, and fixed CBF candidates; ask it to return ten original ISINs.
    15	  Compare `llmrank` with `candidate_order_first10` on identical candidates.
    16	  This adapts LLMRank's sequential/recency prompting, without ICL, bootstrapping,
    17	  or multi-permutation aggregation.
    18	
    19	This README is the primary GitHub guide. Continue with [From HW1 to HW2](HW1_TO_HW2.md)
    20	for questions, exact prompts, input/output formats, and paper references, and
    21	[HW2 results](HW2_RESULTS.md) for the seven-method aggregate comparison.
    22	The optional [HTML handout](BASELINE_GUIDE.html) must be downloaded and opened
    23	locally; GitHub displays its source, not a rendered page. No GitHub Pages hosting
    24	is assumed. Its Markdown companion links are plain text files when opened locally;
    25	read them on GitHub or with a Markdown viewer.

    31	**torch and transformers** installed in your own environment. The optional
    32	[requirements.txt](requirements.txt) preserves the measured pins. For example, in
    33	a user-managed uv project use `uv add 'torch==2.11.0' 'transformers==4.57.6'`;

    98	## Data and evaluation protocol
    99	
   100	Defaults: cutoff **2021-06-01 exclusive**, 30-day future Buy horizon, deterministic
   101	warm-user selection using the starter's SHA256 seed 42 ordering, repeat purchases
   102	allowed, and 50 CBF candidates. Selection never filters by future truth. Eligible
   103	assets need pre-cutoff metadata and a positive historical close price. The starter
   104	excludes exact duplicate transaction rows and reconstructed initial-position rows.
   105	Same-day event ties use ISIN ordering, not invented intraday chronology. Encoder
   106	candidate count does **not** reduce its full eligible corpus.
   107	
   108	Retain and report **Popularity, CBF, Latest buy, and Latest buy or sell** for every
   109	completed run. The starter computes binary nDCG@10, including empty-truth users as
   110	zero in the all-user macro mean; its nonempty-truth mean is reported separately.
   111	Do not change users per method, remove assets to finish generation, or evaluate
   112	partially generated text as a completed encoder benchmark.
   113	
   114	Only as-of source metadata/history/profile information enters prompts; truth is
   115	kept separate. Missing values stay unknown. No future news or external lookup is
   116	supplied, but real public asset names may activate a model's pretrained knowledge.
   117	Generated text is **not automatically factually validated**, and these experiments
   118	are not investment advice.
   119	
   120	## Outputs, failures and resumption
   121	
   122	Completed runs write `predictions.csv`, `metrics.json`, `per_user.json`, and
   123	`run_manifest.json`, preserving all cohort users. `generations.jsonl` records each
   124	request's complete prompt/settings, raw text, tokens and generation time.
   125	`generation_cache/*.json` persists each completed unique request immediately;
   126	identical asset descriptions can share a cache entry, so cache-file count need not
   127	equal completed-asset count. Cache keys bind prompt, model/revision and settings.
   128	Ranker responses also record parse repairs, invalid outputs and fallback decisions.
   129	`ranker_responses.jsonl` is append-only event history: repeated users on resume
   130	are expected, not corruption. On completion, `final_responses.jsonl` contains one
   131	record per current cohort user in manifest order. Runtime `response_log` points
   132	to this canonical file and `history_log` points to the untouched event history.
   133	
   134	The distribution contains source/tests/documentation only, not models, data,
   135	caches, logs, raw customer IDs, or user-level results. Keep generated files in the
   136	ignored `outputs/` directory; do not commit prompts or user-level outputs.
   137	
   138	Default invalid policy is `error`; explicit `--on-invalid fallback` keeps the
   139	original candidate order for an invalid ranker response and original source text
   140	for an invalid encoder paraphrase. These are fallback-inclusive results, **not bare
   141	LLM performance**. Report invalid/fallback and valid-only coverage separately.
   142	
   143	A timed-out encoder retains prompts and cache but has no completed metrics.
   144	A later explicitly authorized run with the **same directory, model and settings**
   145	can reuse compatible cache entries; no automatic retry occurs. Completed encoder
   146	result directories are rejected: choose a fresh directory for a new benchmark.

   135	def contexts_for(users, assets, profiles, history, features, pop, cutoff,
   136	                 candidate_count, exclude_seen):
   137	    contexts, rankings = {}, {}
   138	    for uid in users:
   139	        counts = history.get(uid, Counter())
   140	        eligible = sorted(set(assets) - (set(counts) if exclude_seen else set()))
   141	        if len(eligible) < 10:
   142	            raise ValueError(f'{uid}: fewer than ten eligible assets')
   143	        scores = content_scores(counts, features)
   144	        cold = not counts or not any(scores.values())
   145	        if cold:
   146	            scores = pop
   147	        cbf_ids = order({i: scores[i] for i in eligible})
   148	        pop_ids = order({i: pop[i] for i in eligible})
   149	        asset = lambda isin: {'id': isin, 'name': assets[isin]['assetName'],
   150	                              'attributes': features[isin],
   151	                              'metadata_timestamp': assets[isin]['timestamp']}
   152	        contexts[uid] = {'user_id': uid, 'cutoff': cutoff,
   153	                         'profile': profile_context(profiles[uid]),
   154	                         'history': [dict(asset(i), buy_count=n) for i, n in
   155	                                     sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda p: (-p[1], p[0]))],
   156	                         'candidate_assets': [asset(i) for i in cbf_ids[:candidate_count]],
   157	                         'eligible_asset_ids': eligible,
   158	                         'cold_start': cold}
   159	        rankings[uid] = {'popularity': pop_ids[:10], 'cbf': cbf_ids[:10]}
   160	    return contexts, rankings

   163	def scan_recent_events(data_dir, cutoff, assets):
   164	    """Retained raw events strictly before the cutoff, under load_data's row policy.
   165	
   166	    Exact duplicate full rows are removed, negative transaction IDs (reconstructed
   167	    initial positions) are excluded, and only assets eligible at the cutoff are
   168	    kept.  No row at or after the cutoff enters the result.
   169	    """
   170	    seen, events = set(), defaultdict(list)
   171	    for row in rows(data_dir / 'transactions.csv'):
   172	        key = tuple(sorted(row.items()))
   173	        if key in seen:
   174	            continue
   175	        seen.add(key)
   176	        if int(row['transactionID']) < 0:
   177	            continue
   178	        timestamp = row['timestamp'][:10]
   179	        if timestamp < cutoff and row['ISIN'] in assets:
   180	            events[row['customerID']].append(
   181	                (timestamp, row['ISIN'], row['transactionType']))
   182	    return events

   185	def recency_rankings(contexts, pop, events, k=10):
   186	    # [E6] Latest past Buy (and Buy-or-Sell) dates per asset, ordered by
   187	    # (-last timestamp, ISIN) and filled from the same popularity order.
   188	    rankings = {}
   189	    for uid, context in contexts.items():
   190	        allowed = set(context['eligible_asset_ids'])
   191	        buy_last, any_last = {}, {}
   192	        for timestamp, isin, kind in events.get(uid, ()):
   193	            if isin not in allowed:
   194	                continue
   195	            previous = any_last.get(isin)
   196	            if previous is None or timestamp > previous:
   197	                any_last[isin] = timestamp
   198	            if kind == 'Buy':
   199	                previous = buy_last.get(isin)
   200	                if previous is None or timestamp > previous:
   201	                    buy_last[isin] = timestamp
   202	        pop_order = order({isin: pop[isin] for isin in allowed})
   203	        rankings[uid] = {}
   204	        for method, latest in (('latest_buy', buy_last),
   205	                               ('latest_buy_or_sell', any_last)):
   206	            prefix = sorted(latest, key=lambda isin: (
   207	                -date.fromisoformat(latest[isin]).toordinal(), isin))
   208	            chosen, chosen_set = prefix[:k], set(prefix[:k])
   209	            for isin in pop_order:
   210	                if len(chosen) >= k:
   211	                    break
   212	                if isin not in chosen_set:
   213	                    chosen.append(isin)
   214	                    chosen_set.add(isin)
   215	            rankings[uid][method] = chosen
   216	    return rankings

   153	                }
   154	            else:

   156	                response = generator.generate(prompt, max_new_tokens=MAX_NEW_TOKENS)

# Spreadsheets skill
Read entirely for spreadsheet creation, editing, analysis, or visualization.

## Decision Boundary

## Important Instructions
- For new workbooks or authorized redesigns, plan the simplest correct workbook that meets the task, audience, actual data and domain. If formulas become hard to read, first reconsider whether the workbook’s structure, layout, or logic is overcomplicated before simplifying individual formulas. Remove unnecessary or duplicated logic while preserving calculation correctness, required business relationships, and financial reconciliation
- Instruction precedence for workbook content, layout, and formatting is: user request > reference/template > domain defaults/conventions > general defaults.

## Tools + Contract Requirements
- Author the spreadsheet with `@oai/artifact-tool` JS and only `load_workspace_dependencies` executables/dependencies, never repo-local deps. If unavailable, check `~/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/`. Never modify dependency directories.

- Prefer to patch/rerun one `.mjs` builder. No heredocs or duplicate builders.
- Use the provided API reference for supported syntax. Its examples do not set workbook structure, formatting or formula defaults. Do not inspect package internals or prototypes. If blocked, run at most one targeted `workbook.help("<api_or_feature>")` query.
- No `openpyxl`, `xlsxwriter`, or `pandas.ExcelWriter` authoring unless asked, or  `@oai/artifact-tool` is unavailable.
- Analyze with JS/formulas, else bundled Python (libraries) and JSON/CSV intermediates; other libraries only for missing capabilities.
- Use `update_plan` for complex work.
- In your final response, omit builders, previews, or other support files unless requested.
- For an inline sheet preview in `artifact_session.js`, declare `let previewBytes` before `artifactSession.run(...)`. After editing the sheet inside the callback, capture the PNG with `const preview = await workbook.render({ sheetName, range, format: "png" })` and `previewBytes = await preview.arrayBuffer()`. When the run returns `status: "succeeded"`, call `await nodeRepl.emitImage(previewBytes)`.

## Spreadsheet (Workbook) Complexity: Workbook Structure & Formulas

Keep the workbook simple, especially for focused tasks. A focused task produces a simple analysis, report or tracker for a specific question or workflow. It needs one main output, supported by the necessary inputs and calculations. “Focused” describes the scope of the task, not the number of source records.

Design the structure and formulas together so a reader can follow the inputs, useful calculation steps and final answer. Put summaries and main outputs first, show the work behind them, and avoid tabs or formulas that only repeat finished results. Keep separate schedules and output views when they serve distinct needs. Preserve required detail, the supplied template and the requested edit scope.

## Workbook Structure

### Tab Types & Relationships

Tab types describe the role each part of the workbook plays. They do not require separate tabs. A simple workbook can combine inputs, assumptions, builds and outputs in clearly labeled sections on one worksheet.

**Inputs/Sources and Assumptions feed Builds; Builds calculate results and feed Outputs.** These relationships describe how calculations flow, not the physical tab order. The same rules apply when roles share a tab.

**Input / Sources** contain the data the workbook starts from. Keep dedicated raw source or Actuals areas intact, with original values and source meaning separate from prepared calculations. Cleaning, mapping and source summaries may have their own labeled areas with clear provenance. Put business calculations, including historical calibration from actuals, in the build. Raw source data does not read results back from downstream areas.

**Assumptions** hold the editable drivers and controls used by the builds. When cases are needed, keep one authoritative Case selector on Cover or Assumptions. Group each driver with its `Active Selection` row first, followed by its labeled case inputs, such as Base and Downside, sharing the same period columns. Prefer these driver groups to separate whole-case blocks for new designs. The build links directly to each period's active input. Preserve a supplied layout during narrow edits, and do not add cases or a separate tab when the task does not need them.

Changing the Case selector updates the active forecast assumptions for each period. The same build keeps linking to those active cells and recalculates with the selected values. Outputs update from the build results while historical actuals remain unchanged.

When cases are used, display the selected case on each worksheet by linking to the authoritative selector. Keep only one editable selector; distinguish source actuals and separately labeled comparison cases from the active forecast.

In historical periods, the active assumption row may link to ratios or other measures calculated from actuals in a build. Show that history once, aligned with the build's historical period columns, to help the user set forecast assumptions. The forecast active row selects the chosen case's assumptions and feeds the build. Forecast results must not feed back into the assumptions driving that same forecast. Historical calibration is a business calculation, not a terminal Check/Audit result.

**Build** tabs pull source inputs and assumptions to combine historical analysis, current results and/or a forecast. Bring the relevant inputs and applicable assumptions into clearly labeled rows or columns, then calculate the results on the build. Keep periods aligned and chronological. Show meaningful steps, subtotals and totals so readers can follow the logic—for example, headcount and compensation driving personnel cost, or revenue less COGS producing gross profit. Each step should do useful work. Do not hide the whole calculation in one dense formula or make the build merely repeat finished results from elsewhere.

For a simple calculation, a small labeled assumption block can sit beside it. For a larger build, link important drivers from their control area and show the useful calculation steps. Use one set of forecast schedules driven by the active assumptions, organized by the business sequence, such as revenue, headcount, vendors and cash. Do not mirror the Assumptions grid, add Case columns or parallel named-case forecasts, or apply the selector only to finished results.

A requested case comparison still needs each case's correctly evaluated results. If the requested simultaneous current results cannot be produced with the supported single-build design, explain the limitation and agree on the calculation or refresh method before building the comparison. Do not omit it, link both cases to the active result, or silently substitute snapshots, `TABLE`, arrays, dense formulas or a hidden second build. Preserve explicit user/template requirements and the separately authorized native-feature and capture workflows below.

**Output / Summary** tabs consolidate the builds and tell the main story. These might be named “Overview,” “Summary,” “Exec Summary” or “Dashboard,” depending on the task. Bring across finished build results, show how matching totals roll into higher-level totals and put the main summary above the detail. Readers should be able to trace a headline result to its supporting build without finding the same calculation repeated elsewhere. Keep input retrieval, case selection and detailed business logic in the owning build/control area. Do not route forecast results through Assumptions before presenting them. Historical references used to set drivers and linked case/period displays remain allowed.

**Check / Audit** tabs review source data and builds for completeness, consistency and reconciliation. They may calculate their own diagnostics, but do not own business calculations or feed assumptions, builds or outputs. Nothing outside the check/audit area should depend on its results.

**Cover, if useful** gives a complex workbook a simple front page, especially for recurring or shared workflows. Include the company/project name or available logo, workbook title and relevant period or as-of date, with generous whitespace and restrained branding. Place it first. Keep analysis and methodology off the cover. Skip it for focused tasks or when the main output provides enough context.

For complex workbooks, use a separate `ReadMe` only when source choices, joins, scoring or refresh steps need more explanation than nearby notes. Explain the method and material limitations without repeating outputs or giving a tab tour. Put it last. Multiple sources alone do not require one.

Apply [Style guidance](style_guidelines.md) to these tab and section roles, so formatting helps readers distinguish the main answer, editable inputs and supporting calculations.

### Tab Names

Use concise names that describe each tab's purpose, such as `Check` or `Audit` for a reconciliation tab. Preserve established names during unrelated edits. For new forecast work, use `Forecast review` for review checks, `Forecast variance` for comparisons with a prior forecast, or `Sensitivity` for assumption tests. Do not label these tabs or views `Movement` or `Forecast movement`.

### Tab Order & Progression

For a new workbook or authorized redesign, start with one clear primary view that answers the task. Start with one tab, or two when the original source needs to stay separate, for focused tasks such as a department budget versus actuals report, a peer-company valuation comparison, a weekly marketing campaign report, an appointment-capacity tracker or a research measurement log with unit conversions. Preserve required source tabs and dependencies. Put the requested summary above the supporting detail and calculations. Add another tab only for a distinct source, calculation, reader or workflow need; do not create a separate tab for every role. Keep review commentary, refresh instructions and documentation beside the relevant work when they do not need a separate workflow.

Keep separate schedules when the work requires them, such as revenue, payroll, depreciation and debt builds in a financial model. One or two tabs is a starting point for the examples above, not a limit on every workbook. Do not shrink text, hide necessary calculations or discard records to meet a tab count or fit one printed page. Preserve the supplied template and existing architecture during narrow edits.

| Domain and task | Do: one output tab | Don't: create extra output/build tabs by default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Finance / FP&A: one department's monthly budget versus actuals | On `Budget vs Actuals`, tab name `BvA`, show total spend and variance at the top, with category-level budget, actuals and variance calculations below. | Separate Summary, Dashboard, Scenarios and Assumptions tabs for this report. |
| Financial modeling: peer-company valuation comparison from supplied data | On `Comparable Companies`, tab name `Comps`, show the requested multiple summaries at the top, with peer-company inputs and calculated multiples below. | A DCF, debt schedule or full three-statement model when the task only asks for comparable-company analysis. |
| Marketing: weekly campaign spend and cost per lead | On `Campaigns`, show total spend, leads and overall cost per lead at the top, with campaign detail below. Calculate overall cost per lead from the matching totals. | One output tab per campaign, a duplicate dashboard or an attribution model that wasn't requested. |
| Healthcare administration: appointment capacity by clinic | On `Appointments`, tab name `Appts`, show available slots, bookings and overall utilization at the top, with clinic and period detail below. Calculate overall utilization from the matching totals. | A separate dashboard, clinical alerts or a payroll schedule for an appointment report. |
| Scientific research: measurement log with required unit conversions and a requested summary | On `Measurements`, show the requested results at the top, with original observations, units and required conversions below. | Separate Protocol, Processing, Calculations and Checks tabs, or statistical tests that the task does not require. |

One output worksheet can contain several useful sections. Keep original sources and substantial builds separate when needed; do not create multiple output tabs for the same answer.

For a file with multiple tabs, the physical left-to-right order is **Outputs → Builds → Inputs/Sources/Internal**, with a separate **Assumptions** control panel kept easy to reach, usually just after the primary output and before build tabs. Covers, key outputs (executive summary, financial statements, etc.) belong toward the left; working builds sit in the middle when needed; data, sources, inputs and internal documentation sit toward the right. A two-tab workbook has Output on the left and Input on the right. The logical calculation flow is Source/Input and Assumptions → Build → Output; a visible control panel may sit to the left of its builds. Do not confuse tab position with calculation sequence. Within a horizontal build, factors may feed intermediate results from left to right; preserve chronological period columns. Within a single worksheet, inputs and supporting calculations below can feed the main answer above. Preserve an intentional user/reference layout; do not reorganize a narrow edit to enforce this default.

#### Checks and Audit

Checks/Audit are terminal review areas and are not required for focused tasks. They read source/build evidence and may calculate or summarize their own diagnostics within that area. No formula outside a terminal check/audit area may use its results, directly or through helpers, names or dynamic references. This includes assumptions, business calculations, summaries, presented outputs, displayed statuses and output gates. Keep necessary input validation in the owning input/build logic; checks observe it independently. When separate tabs are useful, keep Checks/Audit and internal documentation toward the right. In complex workbooks, a divider such as `Internal >>` can group them with source data; follow [Style guidance](style_guidelines.md) for divider and child-tab colors. Preserve useful supplied controls and notes, but do not add separate tabs for a few lines.


### Build Structure and Formula Flow

Arrange labeled rows and columns so a reader can follow starting data, assumptions, useful calculation steps, subtotals and results. Follow the physical layout above; the logical sequence of inputs to results does not require every build to run from top to bottom.

- **Row progression:** make the useful business steps visible, such as quantity × rate, capacity used ÷ capacity available, or a balance plus its movements. Link the clean input and applicable assumption into their own labeled rows, then calculate the result on that build. Do not add trivial steps just to create more rows.
- **Active assumptions:** select the active assumptions once in the control area and link each period's cells directly into the same build. Do not bypass the active row, repeat case selection across schedules, put a forecast inside Assumptions or maintain parallel case builds. Resolve a required comparison's calculation and refresh method as described in [Tab Types & Relationships](#tab-types--relationships).
- **Historical reference:** Assumptions may link to historical ratios calculated from actuals in a build to help set forecast drivers. Trace the cells: this actuals-only reference must not create a feedback loop from the forecast into its own assumptions.
- **Column progression:** keep comparable items, scenarios and periods aligned. Use the shared headers and controls described in [Anchoring](#anchoring) and [Dates and Time Periods](#dates-and-time-periods), rather than repeating them beside each calculation.
- **Roll-forwards:** show opening balance, relevant movements and closing balance. Normally link each new period's opening balance to the prior period's closing balance, preserving the model's actual timing and conventions.
- **Reuse:** keep one place that owns each calculation, then link matching results into summaries and useful output views. Apply the matching-input, period, unit, rounding and override conditions in [Formula Construction](#formula-construction).

A tab that only repeats linked values from another tab or workbook is a red flag. Build tabs should perform useful calculations and show the steps. Output tabs should bring results together and calculate relevant subtotals or totals where needed. A useful output may link directly to completed build results without adding new calculations. Keep a linking-only tab when it serves a clear source, import or reporting need; otherwise, combine or remove it within the authorized scope. Do not invent calculations merely to justify a distinct reader view.

### Citation Requirements
These are defaults for new workbooks: user instructions, reference/template conventions and domain guidance take precedence. For edits, follow the workbook’s existing citation practices.
- Cite real sources when they exist.
- Keep citations and sources in one place: an existing input tab (sources or data tab) or in the correct input section in a tab, alongside the input data.
- There are two ways to cite a source:

    - If there is a single source, just have a single cell above the data, left aligned.

3. Retry with minimal patch (not full rewrite).
4. Continue from existing workbook state.

Do not loop indefinitely on similar failures.

     1	# Session 2: MaxSim and MeanSim on FAR-Trans
     2	
     3	Embedding-based reranking with **Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B**, pinned to revision
     4	`97b0c614be4d77ee51c0cef4e5f07c00f9eb65b3`. Teacher code in `shared/` is used unchanged.
     5	
     6	## Method
     7	
     8	Both methods rerank the same 50 CBF candidates using up to five most recent
     9	distinct purchased assets. Asset descriptions contain name, category, subcategory,
    10	sector, industry and market; identifiers and dates are excluded from the text.
    11	Last-token pooling produces 1024-dimensional, L2-normalized embeddings.
    12	
    13	- **MaxSim:** maximum cosine similarity between a candidate and individual history assets.
    14	- **MeanSim:** cosine similarity between a candidate and the normalized mean of history embeddings.
    15	
    16	Evaluation settings: 100 warm users, cutoff **2021-06-01**, a **30-day** evaluation
    17	horizon and Top-10. History and metadata precede the cutoff; future purchases
    18	are used only for evaluation. Repeat recommendations are allowed. Score ties
    19	after rounding to six decimals retain CBF order. Both methods share an embedding cache.
    20	
    21	## Requirements and usage
    22	
    23	Python **3.12** and an Apple Silicon Mac with PyTorch MPS are required.
    24	Dependencies are pinned in `requirements-mps.txt`: torch, transformers, tokenizers,
    25	huggingface-hub, numpy and psutil. Inference uses **MPS, FP16, SDPA, batch 8**;
    26	normalization and cosine arithmetic use FP32. CPU fallback is disabled.
    27	The pinned model must already exist in the local Hugging Face cache.
    28	
    29	Using the existing virtual environment:
    30	
    31	```bash
    32	cd Ivan/session2
    33	export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
    34	
    35	# Unit tests: synthetic inputs, no model inference.
    36	.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -p 'test_*.py' -v
    37	
    38	# Three users; no evaluation against future purchases.
    39	.venv/bin/python run_embeddings.py smoke --output-dir outputs/smoke_new
    40	
    41	# Full 100-user evaluation using the teacher's metrics.
    42	.venv/bin/python run_embeddings.py evaluate --output-dir outputs/evaluate_new
    43	```
    44	
    45	Use a fresh output directory for each run. Optional `--data-dir` and `--cache-dir`
    46	arguments override the default locations. Main code is in `embedding_reranker.py`
    47	and `run_embeddings.py`; tests are in `tests/`, pilot scripts in `experiments/`.
    48	
    49	## Results
    50	
    51	- `results/table_results.csv`: aggregate metrics for four baselines, MaxSim and MeanSim; included in Git.
    52	- `results/final_results/`: unchanged local archive of the completed experiment, including predictions, per-user metrics, protocols, checks and logs; ignored by Git.
    53	- `outputs/`: original runs, intermediate experiments, model and embedding caches; ignored by Git.
    54	- `REPORT_FACTS.txt`: local notes for the separate report; ignored by Git.
